This sequence diagram shows a Pod lifecycle with volume attachment failures in Kubernetes. The operation creates a Pod at 10:04:56, followed by mountVolume starting and MapVolume.MapPodDevice succeeding, but then MapVolume.NodeExpandVolume fails at 10:05:17. Subsequently, unmountDevice operations fail repeatedly (at 10:06:16 and 10:06:17) with the error that the CSI volumeDevice "/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/csi/volumedevices/{pv}/dev" is still referenced from other Pods, triggering reconcile loops.

This diagram illustrates a race condition in Kubernetes controller synchronization across Pod lister, Endpoint lister, and etcd components. At t1 all components show ready state, but at t2 a pod update event causes the Pod lister to transition to "not ready" while the Endpoint lister incorrectly remains "ready" (shown in red), with etcd also showing "notReady" in red. By t3 the Pod lister recovers to "ready" very quickly (xxMS), but the Endpoint lister stays stuck in the "ready" state (red), creating a state mismatch.
